sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Stafford Township?
sections.html:
A Stafford owner can list through an agent, handle the sale without one, or take an as-is offer from a buyer who pays cash. Every path ends at the same municipal checkpoint, a resale Certificate of Occupancy for an existing structure from the township's Office of Inspection.

With 90.3% of homes owner-occupied, a $426,200 median home value and 22.0% of residents aged 65 or older, many Stafford sellers have owned for a long time. A listing gives the widest market and the most time pressure around inspections. A direct sale shortens the calendar and usually leaves repairs to the buyer. Decide which fits before you spend money on touch-ups that the township's visual inspection may not even require.

sections.h2: Where is Stafford Township and what communities does it contain?
sections.html:
Stafford sits on the Jersey Shore in southern Ocean County and stretches from Barnegat Bay west to the Burlington County line. It covers 54.71 square miles, of which 46.12 are land and 8.59 are water, or 15.71% of the total. The ZIP code is 08050 for Manahawkin, and the township borders Barnegat, Eagleswood, Little Egg Harbor, Long Beach Township, Ship Bottom, Surf City and Harvey Cedars.

Stafford is the mainland gateway to Long Beach Island. Route 72 is the only road onto the island and crosses Barnegat Bay on the Manahawkin Bay Bridge into Ship Bottom. The township has these main areas:

  • Manahawkin, the commercial hub around Route 9 and Route 72
  • Beach Haven West, a bayside residential community with 4,143 residents in 2010
  • Ocean Acres, a large residential area shared with Barnegat Township
  • Warren Grove, a rural pocket in the Pine Barrens
  • Bonnet Island, Cedar Bonnet and Mayetta, smaller named places

sections.h2: How did Stafford change from a rural township to a year-round community?
sections.html:
The township was chartered by the Crown on March 3, 1750, carved out of Shrewsbury Township when the area still belonged to Monmouth County. It became one of New Jersey's original townships on February 21, 1798, and joined the newly created Ocean County on February 15, 1850. Over the years it lost land to form what is now Barnegat Township, Eagleswood, Surf City and Long Beach Township.

Growth began in the 1950s with Beach Haven West and Ocean Acres, helped by the Garden State Parkway and a widened Route 72. The 1980s pushed many seasonal cottages into year-round use and brought Stafford Square, the first big shopping center. Population went from 3,684 in 1970 to 10,385 in 1980 and 28,617 in 2020. The practical result for a seller is a stock of 1950s to 1980s houses, some of them converted summer homes, where heating systems and electrical panels draw the township inspector's attention.

sections.h2: What does Stafford inspect before a resale closing?
sections.html:
Under Chapter 81 of the Stafford code, a house that changes occupancy needs an inspection by the Code Official, after which a continuing certificate of occupancy is issued. You submit the Application for Existing Structure Certificate of Occupancy to the Office of Inspection and can reach the office at 609-597-1000, extension 8532. The township describes the review as visual only. It is not a structural investigation, so a buyer will still want a private home inspection.

Three supporting items come with the application:

  • A notarized Heat Certification from the seller or agent confirming a professional inspected the heating system and any solid-fuel burners, which clerical staff will notarize at the counter
  • A letter from the Stafford Municipal Utility Authority confirming water and sewer service, if the house is connected
  • For a private well, a water test by a licensed well driller or tester, approved by the Ocean County Health Department

The township's list of common violations is a useful pre-listing checklist. It includes missing outlet plates and uncovered junction boxes, open spaces in an electrical panel, unsecured fixtures, leaking pipes, relief valves not piped to within 6 inches of the floor, metal dryer vents, house numbers at least 3 inches high, chimney caps, handrails on stairs with more than 3 risers, and guardrails where a deck or stair is 30 inches or more above grade. Smoke detectors are required within 10 feet of sleeping areas and on every floor including the basement, and carbon monoxide detectors are required in one- and two-family homes with fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. See the township's rentals and resales page.

sections.h2: How do flood rules affect a Stafford house sale?
sections.html:
Stafford's house raising page refers to the Base Flood Elevation regulations and to the storm of October 27, 2012, and it describes two permit routes. In the first, the owner raises the home under a construction permit and does not reoccupy it until a Certificate of Occupancy is issued. In the second, the owner repairs the home to safe living conditions first, receives a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy, and raises it later.

Either route needs a zoning permit with a survey showing setbacks and structure height, engineered plans for the new foundation, and releases from every utility serving the building. Insurance Increased Cost of Compliance payments are tied to the permit and the final certificate. A seller with a raised house should keep the permit, engineering sign-off and final certificate in one folder for the buyer's lender. A seller near the bay should ask the Zoning office which flood zone and base flood elevation apply to the address.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and bus lines serve Stafford?
sections.html:
Stafford Township School District covers pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in five schools: Oxycocus, Ronald L. Meinders Primary Learning Center, Ocean Acres Elementary, McKinley Avenue Elementary and Stafford Intermediate. Grades 7 to 12 attend Southern Regional Middle School and Southern Regional High School in Manahawkin. The Marine Academy of Technology and Environmental Science, part of the Ocean County Vocational Technical School, is also in Manahawkin, and St. Mary Academy is a K to 8 Catholic school near the Manahawkin area.

The Garden State Parkway enters from Eagleswood and meets Route 72 at Exit 63, U.S. 9 runs north to south through the center, and County Route 539 crosses the west. NJ Transit's 559 bus runs to Atlantic City, and Ocean Ride routes OC6 and OC10 serve Stafford and Long Beach Island. The Census puts average travel to work at 31.4 minutes.

sections.h2: What state forms and fees come with a Stafford closing?
sections.html: The seller owes New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded, calculated from the price in the deed. The Division of Taxation lists the rates and exemptions on its realty transfer fee page. Shore properties often belong to owners who live elsewhere, so note that a seller who is not a New Jersey resident must prepay estimated Gross Income Tax at closing, never less than 2% of the sale price, unless a listed exception applies. Details are in the GIT/REP FAQ.

faqs.q: Does Stafford require an inspection when a house is sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 81 of the Stafford code calls for an inspection by the Code Official on every change of occupancy, followed by a continuing certificate of occupancy. Apply with the Existing Structure Certificate of Occupancy form.

It is a notarized statement from the seller or the seller's agent that a professional inspected the heating system and any fireplace, wood stove or other solid-fuel burner. The township needs it before it can issue the certificate, and clerical staff can notarize it at the counter.

faqs.q: How is a private well handled in a Stafford sale?
faqs.a: The well water must be tested by a licensed well driller or tester and approved by the Ocean County Health Department. The township asks for that approval in place of the utility letter that houses on public water and sewer provide.

faqs.q: Is the Stafford inspection a full home inspection?
faqs.a: No. The township calls its review visual only and says a complete overview of the property comes from a registered home inspection agency. Buyers usually order their own inspection as well.

faqs.q: What does a Stafford seasonal rental license cost?
faqs.a: The township's seasonal rental page lists a $100 fee, plus $50 for a reinspection. The applicant also supplies proof of paid property taxes, proof of water and sewer payment, and a floor-by-floor drawing. Long-term rentals built before 1978 need lead-based paint inspections.
